title: Terezín Memorial Day Trip from Prague
short_description: A quiet half-day at the Terezín Memorial: the Small Fortress, the former ghetto and the cemeteries, north of Prague. Door to door in your own Mercedes, with your chauffeur waiting and one price for the whole car.
description:
Terezín was built in the 1780s as a fortress town on the Ohře river. During the Second World War the Nazis used it twice: the Small Fortress became a Gestapo police prison, and the walled town became a ghetto through which tens of thousands of Jews from Bohemia, Moravia and across Europe passed on their way to the camps in the east. Today the Terezín Memorial looks after both places and the cemeteries around them.

The Memorial is not one site but several, spread over two areas about a kilometre apart: the Small Fortress with the National Cemetery in front of it, and the town itself with the former Magdeburg Barracks, the Crematorium, the Jewish Cemetery and the Columbarium. A car makes the distance between them easy, and lets you keep the pace the place asks for.

Your chauffeur collects you at your address in Prague and drives you north on the motorway. The car then waits for the time included in your booking, shown next to the price, and moves you between the two areas when you are ready. You can add extra hours when you book. Time beyond your booking on the day is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it.

The price is for the whole car, not per person. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls, parking and the short drives between the Memorial's sites. You see the total before you pay.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a guide. Entrance tickets and guided tours are not included. The Memorial runs its own guided tours of the Small Fortress in several languages, and only Memorial guides or guides it authorises may lead visitors inside the fortress. If you would like one, book it with the Memorial in advance and we will time the day around it.
highlights: The Small Fortress, a Gestapo police prison from 1940 to 1945, with its cells, courtyards and fortification corridor
The National Cemetery in front of the fortress, where the remains of thousands of victims lie
The former Magdeburg Barracks, seat of the ghetto's Jewish self-government, with exhibitions on music, art and theatre in the ghetto
The Crematorium and the Jewish Cemetery outside the town walls
A car between the Small Fortress and the town, about a kilometre apart
A pace of your own, without a group or a coach timetable

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Prague address
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your hotel or apartment in Prague at the time you chose. Most visitors leave in the morning, so the day at the Memorial is not rushed.

itinerary.title: Drive north to Terezín
itinerary.body: The road follows the D8 motorway north through the flat farmland of the Elbe valley. Terezín lies a few minutes from the motorway exit.

itinerary.title: The Small Fortress and the National Cemetery
itinerary.body: Start where most visitors start: the National Cemetery in front of the fortress, then the gate and the prison inside. Walk the route on your own, or join a Memorial guide you booked in advance. The documentary in the fortress cinema is a good introduction.

itinerary.title: To the former ghetto
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur drives you into the town, about a kilometre away. The former Magdeburg Barracks, with its exhibitions and a reconstructed dormitory, is the place to begin here.

itinerary.title: The Crematorium and the cemeteries
itinerary.body: Outside the town walls stand the Crematorium and the Jewish Cemetery, and nearby the Columbarium and the ceremonial halls. They are a short walk from each other, or a short drive.

itinerary.title: Back to the car
itinerary.body: Call or message your chauffeur when you are ready. The car is waiting where you were dropped off, and the drive back is quiet if you prefer it to be.

itinerary.title: Return to your Prague address
itinerary.body: The same car and chauffeur bring you back to the same address in Prague where the day began, usually in time for a late lunch.

includes: A private Mercedes with your own chauffeur, for your party only
Pickup and return at your address in Prague
The drive to Terezín and back, and the short drives between the Small Fortress and the town
Waiting time at the destination for the hours included in your booking
Child seats at no charge: tell us the children’s ages when you book
One price for the whole car, shown in full before you pay
excludes: Entrance tickets to the Memorial, which are bought on site
A guide or a guided tour: your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide
Extra hours beyond your booking, unless you add them when you book
pickup_info: Pickup and return are at your address in Prague: a hotel, an apartment or an office. Tell us the exact address when you book. Before the day you receive your chauffeur’s name and phone number, and on the day they wait at the door at the agreed time. A morning start suits the Memorial best, as the Small Fortress and the town sites close in the late afternoon, and earlier in winter.
important_info:
The Terezín Memorial is a place of remembrance. Visitors are asked to keep quiet, stay on the marked route and not eat or drink inside the buildings. Photography for personal use is allowed, but not with flash, tripods or selfie sticks indoors, and not where signs or staff say otherwise.

The Memorial is several separate sites. The Small Fortress and the town are about a kilometre apart, each with its own car park. Your chauffeur drives you between them.

The Crematorium, the Columbarium and the ceremonial halls are closed on Saturdays. All sites are closed on 24, 25 and 26 December and on 1 January, and close early on 23 and 31 December. The Ghetto Museum is closed for reconstruction; a temporary exhibition on the history of the ghetto is on show in the former Magdeburg Barracks. Check the Memorial’s opening times before you travel.

Tickets are bought on site, by card or cash. Guided tours of the Small Fortress are run by the Memorial and booked with it in advance.

Your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide. Entrance tickets and guided tours are not included.

faq.q: How is the price worked out?
faq.a: There is one price for the whole car, set for each car class. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls, parking, the short drives between the Memorial’s sites and the hours at the destination included in your booking. You can add extra hours when you book, and you see the total before you pay.

faq.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faq.a: Yes. The same car and chauffeur take you to Terezín, wait for the time you booked, drive you between the Small Fortress and the town, and bring you back to your Prague address. Waiting during the hours in your booking is part of the price.

faq.q: Can we have a guide at the Small Fortress?
faq.a: Yes, through the Memorial. Only Memorial guides or guides it authorises may lead visitors inside the Small Fortress, and the Memorial offers tours in several languages. Book the tour with the Memorial in advance and tell us the time, so we plan the pickup around it.

The Ghetto Museum is closed for reconstruction. While it is closed, a temporary exhibition on the history of the ghetto is on show in the former Magdeburg Barracks, which is also where tickets for the town sites are sold. Check the Memorial’s website for the reopening.

The Memorial publishes no age limit, and families do visit. Some exhibitions describe suffering and death plainly, so parents usually decide by the child’s age and readiness. Children under ten enter free, and child seats in the car are at no charge.

faq.q: What if we want to stay longer on the day?
faq.a: Tell your chauffeur. Time beyond your booking is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it, at the same extra-hour price you saw when you booked. Nothing is charged automatically.

faq.q: How many people fit in one car?
faq.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
